scenario.title: Pizza, Clay & Laser Spears
scenario.tagline: Pizza / Keramzyt / Kebab / Laser spears / Starships / Renovation
scenario.description: A pizza chain and a keramzyt factory open the season in the Republic of Valdoria - and every 2 weeks a new company joins the exchange. Read the news, check each company's hard data, watch for delayed effects and keep enough money for rent - in cash or in the safe savings vault.

companies.name: Cosmic Pizza
companies.main_product: Pizza delivered anywhere in the system, still hot
companies.description: A pizza chain with 64 restaurants and a fleet of delivery pods across Valdoria and its moon. Famous for its meteor-crust pepperoni and a hot sauce nobody has managed to copy. Restaurants buy their flour, cheese and meat on monthly contracts.
companies.condition: Steady and profitable. Flour, cheese and meat make up almost half of its costs, so food prices matter a lot.
companies.fine_print: Flour, cheese and meat are bought on monthly contracts, so price changes reach the menu weeks later.

companies.name: Fabric of Keramzyt
companies.main_product: Keramzyt - light clay pebbles baked in giant kilns, used in walls, floors and space bases
companies.description: The biggest keramzyt maker in the northern provinces. It digs clay, bakes it into light, bubbly pebbles in gas-fired rotary kilns and sells them to builders on long contracts.
companies.condition: Reliable and a bit boring - in a good way. Pays regular dividends, but depends on the building season and on energy prices for its kilns.
companies.fine_print: The kilns run on gas: energy taxes and gas prices hit profits right away.

companies.name: Galac-Kebab
companies.main_product: Kebabs for every species, including a zero-gravity döner
companies.description: A fast-growing kebab chain with stands at spaceports, mines and night markets. Its new Zero-G Döner is wrapped so tightly that nothing floats away on orbital stations.
companies.condition: Promising new products waiting for food-safety approval. Loyal fans, but modest profits so far - a bit risky.
companies.fine_print: The Zero-G Döner still needs a food-safety approval. Such decisions usually take about two weeks.

companies.name: Laser Dzida Works
companies.main_product: Laser spears (dzidas) for space rangers and moon-base guards
companies.description: A fast-growing weapons maker that builds laser spears - 'dzidas' - for rangers, guards and collectors. Every spear is assembled in one large factory on the edge of Port Lumen.
companies.condition: Growing fast, but it borrowed a lot of money and relies on a single factory for everything it sells.
companies.fine_print: Every spear is built in one single factory. $46M of loans must be refinanced with the bank this season.

companies.name: Howl Starships
companies.main_product: Cargo starships with famously loud engines
companies.description: A young shipyard that builds cargo starships for traders flying between Valdoria and its moon. Its ships are cheap and tough - and you can hear them howl from three valleys away.
companies.condition: A young company with big loans for its shipyard. Very sensitive to trade, strikes and orders - clearly risky.
companies.fine_print: Young shipyard: its share price usually swings about twice as much as the market (high volatility).

companies.name: Łęcicki Renovations
companies.main_product: Flat finishing and renovations: tiles, plaster, paint and 'it'll be done by Monday'
companies.description: A 40-year-old family firm that finishes and renovates flats, offices and space-station cabins. Always busy, always slightly late, and known for steady, generous dividends.
companies.condition: Very safe: a big order book and loyal customers. Gets more work when people fix up old homes instead of buying new ones.
companies.fine_print: Customers pay before the work starts - online reviews have never changed the order book.

events.title: Record number of students enrol at Valdoria's universities
events.description: Universities report 40% more first-year students than last year. The semester starts in two weeks - and the dorm kitchens have one hot plate per floor.

effects.consequence_text: The student wave from Week 1 moved into the dorms - late-night pizza orders exploded and Cosmic Pizza's shares followed.

events.title: Long dry spell forecast - builders rush to start
events.description: Forecasters expect weeks of dry, warm weather starting next week. Construction firms across Valdoria are moving their projects forward.

effects.consequence_text: The dry spell forecast in Week 1 arrived - building sites ordered keramzyt by the truckload and Fabric of Keramzyt's shares rose.
cause_chain: Dry weather is on the way

events.title: Celebrity chef: 'Pizza is so last season'
events.description: TV chef Rocco Vantelli told a talk show that pizza is 'out' and that 'everyone will be eating foam and moss by spring'. The clip has 3 million views.

events.title: Parliament raises the energy excise tax
events.description: Lawmakers voted to raise the excise tax on electricity and gas by 20%, starting next week. Landlords warn that the cost of heating and lighting buildings will be passed on to tenants.

effects.consequence_text: The energy excise voted in Week 2 just reached your landlord's bills - your monthly rent went up by $80.
cause_chain: Landlords pass it on to tenants

effects.consequence_text: Keramzyt is baked in gas-fired kilns - investors expected pricier energy to eat its profits, and the shares slipped right away.
cause_chain: Gas-fired kilns cost more to run

events.title: Fabric of Keramzyt reports a record quarter
events.description: Fabric of Keramzyt sold more clay pebbles than ever this quarter. The board announced that dividend payments to shareholders will go up starting next week.

effects.consequence_text: Record profits lifted Fabric of Keramzyt's share price as soon as the results were published.
The bigger dividend promised in Week 2 kicked in - Fabric of Keramzyt now pays shareholders more cash every week.
cause_chain: The board shares more cash with owners

events.title: Viral post: 'Keramzyt pebbles are alien eggs'
events.description: A post claiming that keramzyt pebbles 'hatch at night' was shared 500,000 times. Geologists call it complete nonsense - it's baked clay.

events.title: Galac-Kebab lists on the Galactic Exchange
events.description: The kebab chain sold its first shares at $50. Its new Zero-G Döner is waiting for food-safety approval for orbital stations - a decision is expected in about two weeks.

effects.consequence_text: Hungry investors bought Galac-Kebab in its first week - the price edged up.
cause_chain: A new company joins the exchange

effects.consequence_text: The Zero-G Döner approval expected since Week 3 came through. Galac-Kebab can now sell it on every orbital station - and its share price jumped.

events.title: Pizza cooks and couriers win a higher minimum wage
events.description: After long negotiations, restaurant staff and delivery couriers in Valdoria will earn 12% more starting next week. Owners say they will have to raise menu prices or accept smaller profits.

effects.consequence_text: The higher wages agreed in Week 3 showed up in restaurant costs - Cosmic Pizza's profits shrank and its share price dipped.
Bigger wage bills from Week 3 made Cosmic Pizza trim its dividend by a quarter.
Bigger wage bills from Week 3 squeezed Cosmic Pizza's cash - its bankruptcy risk crept up.

events.title: Rumor: a foreign giant wants to buy Cosmic Pizza
events.description: An anonymous forum user claims a huge foreign food group is about to buy Cosmic Pizza at a big premium. Neither company has commented.

cosmic-pizza.fine_print: New wage rules apply from this week. The dividend is reviewed every week.

events.title: Hostile aliens launch a takeover of Fabric of Keramzyt
events.description: A fleet of grumpy aliens from the Glutonian Empire bought 30% of the shares overnight. They demand that the kilns bake 'edible pebbles' and have parked a battle cruiser over the clay pit.

effects.consequence_text: The hostile takeover attempt scared investors - Fabric of Keramzyt shares dipped right away.
cause_chain: Investors fear chaos at the kilns

events.title: Falafel craze sweeps the galaxy
events.description: A pop star's falafel diet went viral, and half of Valdoria now orders chickpea balls instead of meat. Kebab stands report long, quiet evenings.

effects.consequence_text: Customers switched to falafel - Galac-Kebab's sales and shares dipped the same week.
Cold grills ate into Galac-Kebab's cash - its risk went up.

events.title: Gossip: Galac-Kebab boss spotted on a luxury yacht
events.description: A celebrity magazine printed blurry photos of someone who 'looks like' Galac-Kebab's founder at a yacht party. The company says he was at a food fair that day.

events.title: Laser Dzida Works lists and unveils a brand-new technology
events.description: The laser-spear maker sold its first shares at $80 and showed off the Dzida-3000: the first spear with a laser tip that 'never needs sharpening'. 40,000 rangers pre-ordered it in 48 hours. Every spear is built in one single factory.

effects.consequence_text: Investors loved the new laser-tip technology - Laser Dzida Works rose in its very first week.

events.title: Drought hits the southern farm belt
events.description: Two months without rain in the south. Farmers warn that wheat and tomato harvests will be smaller and ingredients will cost more in a couple of weeks.

effects.consequence_text: The drought from Week 5 finally pushed up flour and tomato costs - pizza profits shrank.
cause_chain: Drought shrinks wheat and tomato harvests

effects.consequence_text: Pricier ingredients after the Week 5 drought added a little risk to Cosmic Pizza.

events.title: Astrologer: 'A golden week for building stocks'
events.description: A popular astrologer told her 2 million followers that 'Jupiter is smiling on anything made of clay' this week.

keramzyt.fine_print: The moon kiln is paid for with a $22M loan. First pebbles are expected in about three weeks.

galac-kebab.fine_print: Approved for every orbital station. Most sales still come from spaceports and night markets.

events.title: Testing the new laser tip sets the factory on fire
events.description: An engineer tested the Dzida-3000's new laser tip indoors 'just for a second'. Nobody was hurt, but Laser Dzida Works' only factory in Port Lumen burned down to the walls and all deliveries are on hold.

effects.consequence_text: The factory fire hit Laser Dzida Works immediately - investors sold the same week, expecting months without sales.
With its only factory offline and loans to repay, Laser Dzida Works' bankruptcy risk jumped.
cause_chain: No sales, but loans still due

events.title: Fabric of Keramzyt builds a giant kiln on the moon
events.description: Construction starts now; the new moon kiln should bake its first pebbles for space-base builders in about three weeks.

effects.consequence_text: At first, investors worried about the building costs.
cause_chain: A huge moon kiln to build

effects.consequence_text: The moon kiln announced in Week 6 started production - Fabric of Keramzyt's shares jumped.
Fabric of Keramzyt borrowed heavily to build the moon kiln - its bankruptcy risk rose.
cause_chain: The kiln is built with borrowed money

effects.consequence_text: With the moon kiln earning money since Week 9, Fabric of Keramzyt's debt looks safer.

events.title: Online trend: 'Laser spears can cut through time'
events.description: A viral video claims a Dzida-3000 sliced 'a hole into last Tuesday'. Weapon reviewers point out that the video is satire.

laser-dzida.fine_print: The insurance payout for the fire is not guaranteed. Loan payments are still due every week.

events.title: Howl Starships lists on the Galactic Exchange
events.description: The shipyard sold its first shares at $30. Its founders promise 'loud engines, reliable ships'.

effects.consequence_text: Howl's first week of trading ended a little above its listing price.
cause_chain: A new shipyard joins the exchange

events.title: Laser Dzida Works' insurer disputes the fire claim
events.description: The insurance company says the factory tested lasers indoors against safety rules and may refuse to pay for the damage. Lawyers expect a long fight.

effects.consequence_text: News of the insurance dispute pushed Laser Dzida Works shares lower right away.
cause_chain: The insurer may refuse to pay
No money to rebuild the factory

effects.consequence_text: The insurance dispute from Week 7 turned into real cash trouble - without a payout, Laser Dzida Works' bankruptcy risk climbed again.

events.title: Meme: 'Cosmic Pizza cures Monday blues'
events.description: A cartoon claiming Cosmic Pizza 'fixes bad moods' was shared a million times.

laser-dzida.fine_print: The bank has halved the credit line. Without new money, bills can't be paid for long.

howl.fine_print: An $8M loan pays for the new Star Inquisition shipyard, due to open in about two weeks.

events.title: Bank cuts Laser Dzida Works' credit line
events.description: Valdoria Merchant Bank halved the amount Laser Dzida Works is allowed to borrow. Without new money, the company may struggle to pay suppliers and rebuild its factory.

effects.consequence_text: Losing its bank credit sent Laser Dzida Works shares down immediately.
cause_chain: The bank cuts the credit line

effects.consequence_text: The credit cut from Week 8 left Laser Dzida Works unable to pay its bills - its bankruptcy risk crossed the danger line.

events.title: Howl builds a new shipyard for the Star Inquisition
events.description: The Star Inquisition - the fleet's strictest and grumpiest order - needs 40 new patrol ships. Howl's new shipyard will open in about two weeks to build them.

effects.consequence_text: The Star Inquisition shipyard announced in Week 8 opened - patrol-ship orders flowed in and Howl's shares took off.
cause_chain: A new shipyard opens to build them
A big order means more sales

effects.consequence_text: A long contract with the Star Inquisition made Howl's loans easier to repay.

events.title: Tourists 'see a UFO' over Howl's test field
events.description: Blurry phone videos show a glowing dot above the shipyard's test field. Fans call it 'proof of alien customers'.

events.title: Łęcicki Renovations lists its shares
events.description: The family renovation firm sold shares to the public for the first time. Its work is famously bad - but customers always pay, and Łęcicki simply moves on to a district where nobody knows him yet.

effects.consequence_text: Łęcicki's debut was calm - the money keeps coming in, whatever the walls look like.

events.title: Central bank raises interest rates
events.description: To slow rising prices, the central bank raised its main interest rate. Mortgages and big building projects get more expensive.

effects.consequence_text: Higher rates mean fewer new buildings - Fabric of Keramzyt slipped right away.
cause_chain: Mortgages and big builds cost more

effects.consequence_text: With new flats too expensive after the Week 9 rate rise, Valdorians fixed up their old ones instead - Łęcicki's order book filled up.
Higher interest rates make Fabric of Keramzyt's moon-kiln loans more expensive.
The central bank's rate rise from Week 9 reached your bank - your savings account now pays more interest every week.
cause_chain: The central bank raises its rate

events.title: Review portal: Łęcicki gets 1.1 stars
events.description: 'The tiles fell off after a week.' 'He painted my cat.' Nobody on Valdoria recommends Łęcicki to anyone. Commenters predict the end of the firm.

events.title: Housing board approves a building maintenance fee
events.description: Apartment buildings will add $40 a month to rent in about two weeks to repair old elevators.

effects.consequence_text: The maintenance fee approved in Week 10 has been added to your rent: +$40 a month.
cause_chain: The fee lands in your rent

events.title: Howl shipyard welders go on strike
events.description: Half-built starships are standing still at Howl's shipyard. The union says the strike could last several weeks.

effects.consequence_text: The strike froze Howl's deliveries the same week - its shares fell.
Weeks without finished ships mean weeks without income - Howl's risk went up.

events.title: Rumor: a ghost haunts the keramzyt kiln
events.description: Night-shift workers joked about 'spooky noises' in the kiln hall. The story went viral.

events.title: Łęcicki moves to a brand-new moon colony
events.description: Nobody on Valdoria will hire him twice, so Łęcicki is moving to the new moon colony: 10,000 fresh flats need finishing, and nobody there has heard of him yet. A bigger dividend starts next week.

effects.consequence_text: Łęcicki's bigger dividend promised in Week 11 is now being paid out.

events.title: The Galactic Cup final comes to Valdoria
events.description: Fans of two planets are flying in for the final. Every fan zone will be next to a Galac-Kebab stand, and the chain promises a bigger dividend from next week.

effects.consequence_text: Hungry football fans emptied every kebab grill - Galac-Kebab shares rose the same week.
cause_chain: Kebab stands in every fan zone

effects.consequence_text: Galac-Kebab's bigger dividend promised in Week 11 is now being paid.
Record fan-zone sales gave Galac-Kebab a fat cash cushion - its risk fell.

events.title: Celebrity diet: 'Only eat purple food'
events.description: A pop star says she eats only purple food now. Nutrition experts are not impressed.

events.title: Galac-Kebab becomes the official kebab of the Galactic League
events.description: Stadiums on Kestria, Nordhavia and the Solmara Islands will serve only Galac-Kebab to fans for the next two years - the chain's biggest deal ever.

effects.consequence_text: The league deal lifted Galac-Kebab shares the same week it was announced.
Two years of stadium crowds give Galac-Kebab a safer, steadier income.

events.title: Łęcicki pays a year-end bonus dividend
events.description: A strong year lets Łęcicki add a one-off bonus to this week's dividend.

effects.consequence_text: Łęcicki's year-end bonus was added to this week's dividend.

events.title: Rumor: Galac-Kebab and Howl to merge into 'Kebab-Howl Express'
events.description: A gossip site claims the two companies will 'fly kebabs into orbit at full howl'. Both deny it.

w1-noise-chef.reveal: One TV chef's opinion doesn't change how many pizzas people actually order. Cosmic Pizza's sales were not affected.
misleading_chain: A TV chef says pizza is out

w2-noise-clouds.reveal: Keramzyt is baked clay - nothing hatches. A viral post isn't evidence: always ask who is behind a claim.
misleading_chain: A viral post calls pebbles alien eggs

w3-noise-takeover.reveal: No buyer ever showed up - the 'takeover' was an anonymous rumor. If Cosmic Pizza rose this week, it was thanks to the students from Week 1 moving into the dorms.
misleading_chain: A giant may buy Cosmic Pizza

w4-noise-yacht.reveal: A blurry gossip photo says nothing about how a company is doing. Galac-Kebab's founder was at a food fair.
misleading_chain: The boss is seen on a yacht

w5-noise-astro.reveal: Horoscopes don't set share prices. Fabric of Keramzyt moved because of real news - the dry spell, its record quarter and the alien takeover attempt.
misleading_chain: An astrologer predicts a golden week
Her fans may rush to buy

w6-noise-fridge.reveal: The video was a joke. Laser Dzida Works' real problem this week was the factory fire caused by its own new technology.
misleading_chain: Video: spears cut holes in time

w7-noise-meme.reveal: A funny meme doesn't sell more pizza. Cosmic Pizza was really moved by students, wages and food prices.
misleading_chain: A meme says pizza cures Mondays

w8-noise-ufo.reveal: A glowing dot in a blurry video isn't a customer. Howl's real news was the Star Inquisition shipyard.
misleading_chain: A UFO over the test field

w9-noise-reviews.reveal: Bad reviews didn't change the money: customers always pay, and Łęcicki just moves on to a district where nobody has read them. His income stayed exactly the same.

w10-noise-ghost.reveal: There is no ghost - just a noisy old kiln. Fabric of Keramzyt's real story was its moon kiln.

w11-noise-diet.reveal: One celebrity's diet doesn't change what millions of people eat.
misleading_chain: A pop star eats only purple food

w12-noise-merger.reveal: There was no merger - both companies denied it, and nothing changed.

week_lesson.title_delayed: Old news just hit the market
week_lesson.title_quiet: A calm week on the market
week_lesson.summary_no_moves: Share prices barely moved this week.
week_lesson.lag_with_delayed: Markets don't always react the moment news breaks. Restaurants buy ingredients on monthly contracts, new laws start later and bills arrive weeks after a decision - so an effect can land long after the headline. This week: {items}.
week_lesson.lag_without_delayed: Nothing from older news landed this week - but stay alert. Some headlines need one, two or even three weeks to reach a company's costs, its profits or your own bills. Re-read earlier news before you trade.
week_lesson.immediate_note: Some news moved prices the very same week: {items}.
week_lesson.noise_note: Not every headline matters: {items} turned out to be noise and changed nothing.
week_lesson.rent_change_note: Your monthly rent changed by {delta} (now {rent}) because of news from Week {source_week}.
week_lesson.rent_paid_note: You paid {amount} in rent this week.
week_lesson.dividend_note: Your shares paid you {amount} in dividends - cash just for owning them.
week_lesson.bankruptcy_note: {names} went bankrupt. Its shares are now worth $0 and can no longer be traded.
week_lesson.takeaway_delayed: Today's headline can be next month's price move. Before you trade, look back at older news.
week_lesson.takeaway_immediate: Big surprises, like disasters, hit prices right away. Spreading your money across companies softens the blow.
week_lesson.takeaway_quiet: Calm weeks are a good moment to check your plan and your cash reserve for upcoming bills.
week_lesson.savings_note: Your savings account paid you {amount} in interest ({rate} of your balance) - small, but completely safe.
week_lesson.savings_rent_note: Your cash was short on rent day, so {amount} moved automatically from savings - exactly what a bill buffer is for.
week_lesson.savings_rate_note: Interest rates rose because of news from Week {source_week}: your savings now earn {new} a week instead of {old}.

glossary.Market lag: The delay between a piece of news and its effect on prices. Some news needs weeks to show up.
glossary.Dividend: Cash a company pays to its shareholders, just for owning its shares.
glossary.Share price: What one small piece of a company costs right now.
glossary.Bankruptcy risk: How likely a company is to run out of money. If it goes bankrupt, its shares can become worthless.
glossary.Liquidity: How much cash you can use right away - for example, to pay your rent.
glossary.Noise: News that sounds important but doesn't actually change anything.
glossary.Diversification: Spreading your money across different companies and industries, so one bad event can't sink you.
glossary.ROI: Return on investment: how much your money grew or shrank, shown in percent.
glossary.Excise tax: An extra tax on specific products, such as fuel or electricity.
glossary.Savings account: A bank account that keeps your money safe and pays you a little interest for leaving it there.
glossary.Interest: Money a bank pays you for keeping your savings with it - or that you pay when you borrow.
glossary.Interest rate: The percentage a bank pays (or charges) for money. When the central bank raises it, savings earn more and loans cost more.
glossary.Profit margin: How many cents of every dollar of sales a company keeps as profit.
glossary.Debt: Money a company has borrowed and must pay back, usually with interest.
glossary.Emergency fund: Savings kept only for bills and surprises, so you never have to sell investments in a hurry.

advisor.accurate_delayed: Keep an eye on {company} ({ticker}). '{event}' could {direction} its price {timing}. Markets often need time to catch up with news.
advisor.accurate_immediate: '{event}' looks important for {company} ({ticker}). I'd expect it to {direction} the price {timing}.
advisor.accurate_risk: Careful with {company} ({ticker}). After '{event}', its money problems look serious - if a company goes bankrupt, its shares can be worth nothing.
advisor.accurate_dividend: '{event}' could change how much {company} ({ticker}) pays its shareholders {timing}. Dividends add up week after week.
advisor.accurate_rent: '{event}' may not move share prices much, but it could make your bills bigger {timing}. Keep some cash ready for rent.
advisor.misleading_noise: Big news! '{event}' could really {direction} the price of {company} ({ticker}) - and fast. If I were you, I'd act this week.
advisor.misleading_inverted: I have a feeling about {company} ({ticker}): after '{event}', I think the market will {direction} its price. Trust me on this one.
advisor.quiet_week: Honestly, I don't see anything big this week. Sometimes the smartest move is to stick to your plan and keep cash for bills.
advisor.accurate_savings: '{event}' matters for your own money, not a company: your savings account could pay more interest {timing}. Safe money earns a bit more when rates go up.
quiet_chain: Stick to your plan, keep a bill buffer

cautious.label: Cautious Saver
cautious.description: You kept most of your money in cash. That's safe and kept your bills covered, but cash alone doesn't grow or earn dividends.

balanced.label: Balanced Diversifier
balanced.description: You spread your money across several companies and kept some cash aside. That's how many long-term investors protect themselves from surprises.

concentrated.label: Focused Bettor
concentrated.description: You put most of your money into one company at a time. When the pick is right it pays off big - but one bad headline can hurt a lot.

aggressive.label: Bold Go-Getter
aggressive.description: You kept nearly all your money invested and traded often. Bold moves can pay off, but they leave little room for bills and surprises.

reactive.label: Headline Chaser
reactive.description: You reacted quickly to the news - including headlines that turned out to be noise. Speed only helps when the news is real.

diversify.title: Spread your bets
diversify.tip: Own a few companies from different industries. One fire, lawsuit or bad quarter shouldn't sink your whole savings.

cash_reserve.title: Keep a bill buffer
cash_reserve.tip: Before investing, set aside enough cash for upcoming bills like rent. Money you'll need soon shouldn't be stuck in shares.

delayed_signals.title: Read yesterday's news
delayed_signals.tip: Many effects arrive late - contracts, laws and prices take weeks to pass through. Ask: 'What happened two weeks ago that hasn't shown up yet?'

noise.title: Check the source
noise.tip: Rumors, gossip and viral posts are usually noise. Ask who is saying it and whether it changes the company's real sales or costs.

bankruptcy.title: Respect the warning lights
bankruptcy.tip: When a company's bankruptcy risk keeps climbing, shrink your stake. A cheap-looking share can still fall to zero.

dividends.title: Let dividends work for you
dividends.tip: Steady companies that pay dividends hand you cash regularly - even in weeks when prices stand still.

advisor.title: Trust, but verify
advisor.tip: Advisors and experts can be wrong. Treat a hint as one opinion and compare it with the actual news before you act.

patience.title: Have a plan, not a reflex
patience.tip: Decide why you are buying before you buy. A few well-reasoned trades usually beat many quick ones.

savings.title: Give every dollar a job
savings.tip: Money for bills goes into a savings account, money you won't need for years can be invested. Cash lying around does neither.

final_analysis.overall_positive: You finished with {net_worth} - a {roi} return. Great job turning headlines into decisions!
final_analysis.overall_neutral: You finished with {net_worth} ({roi}). You protected your money - next time, let's make it grow a little smarter.
final_analysis.overall_negative: You finished with {net_worth} ({roi}). Losing money in a game is the cheapest way to learn - here is what to try next time.
final_analysis.overall_liquidity: You ran out of cash for rent in Week {week}. That ends the game - but it's one of the most valuable lessons in personal finance: bills come first.

s_diversified.title: You spread your money out
s_diversified.detail: You owned {count} different companies across {industries} industries. When one stock stumbled, the others cushioned the fall.

s_caught_delayed.title: You were in place before old news hit
s_caught_delayed.detail: You held {shares} {ticker} shares when '{event}' (Week {source_week}) finally moved the price in Week {trigger_week} ({impact}). That's how patient investors profit from market lag.

s_dodged_delayed.title: You dodged a delayed hit
s_dodged_delayed.detail: You sold {ticker} after '{event}' appeared in Week {source_week} - before it pulled the price down in Week {trigger_week}.

s_cash_reserve.title: You kept money ready for the bills
s_cash_reserve.detail: You had {cash} ready in cash and savings before the {rent} rent payment in Week {week}. The bill never caught you off guard.

s_exited_risk.title: You left a sinking ship in time
s_exited_risk.detail: You sold your {ticker} shares before the company went bankrupt in Week {week}.

s_avoided_bankrupt.title: You avoided the bankruptcy
s_avoided_bankrupt.detail: You held no {ticker} shares when it went bankrupt in Week {week}. Watching the risk meter pays off.

s_ignored_noise.title: You didn't fall for the noise
s_ignored_noise.detail: None of your trades followed the {count} misleading headlines. Staying calm when rumors fly is a real skill.

s_dividends.title: Your shares paid you
s_dividends.detail: You collected {amount} in dividends - money that arrived without selling a single share.

s_profit.title: You grew your money
s_profit.detail: You finished with {net_worth}, a return of {roi}, after paying all your bills.

s_finished.title: You stayed in the game
s_finished.detail: You made it through all {weeks} weeks and saw how news, delays and bills shape your money.

i_concentrated.title: Too many eggs in one basket
i_concentrated.detail: At one point {share} of your stock money sat in {ticker} alone. Spreading across industries limits the damage when one company gets hit.

i_missed_delayed.title: The early signal was there
i_missed_delayed.detail: '{event}' appeared in Week {source_week}, but {ticker} only reacted in Week {trigger_week} ({impact}). Buying in between would have caught that move.

i_hit_delayed.title: Old news caught up with you
i_hit_delayed.detail: You held {shares} {ticker} shares when '{event}' from Week {source_week} pulled the price down in Week {trigger_week} ({impact}). Re-reading older headlines could have warned you.

i_immediate_hit.title: One shock, a big dent
i_immediate_hit.detail: You held {shares} {ticker} shares when '{event}' hit in Week {week} and lost about {loss}. Owning several companies would have softened the blow.

i_low_cash.title: Rent nearly caught you
i_low_cash.detail: Before the {rent} rent payment in Week {week} you had only {cash} in cash and savings. Keep a cushion for bills you know are coming.

i_liquidity.title: Out of cash on rent day
i_liquidity.detail: After paying {rent} rent in Week {week} your cash fell to {cash}, and your savings were empty. Shares are not cash - sell in time or keep a reserve in savings.

i_bankrupt_loss.title: Held on until the very end
i_bankrupt_loss.detail: You still owned {shares} {ticker} shares when it went bankrupt in Week {week} - about {loss} turned into $0. A 'Critical' risk label is a signal to reduce your stake.

i_followed_noise.title: A rumor moved your money
i_followed_noise.detail: In Week {week} you {action} {ticker} right after '{event}' - a headline that turned out to be noise.

i_followed_bad_advice.title: The advisor got it wrong
i_followed_bad_advice.detail: In Week {week} the advisor's hint about {ticker} was a misread, and you {action} after it. Even experts are wrong sometimes - double-check hints against the news.

i_idle_cash.title: Your cash sat on the bench
i_idle_cash.detail: On average only {share} of your money was invested, and most of the rest was plain cash. Even the savings vault would have paid interest on it.

i_overtrading.title: Lots of trades, lots of noise
i_overtrading.detail: You made {count} trades in {weeks} weeks. Frequent trading often means reacting to every headline instead of following a plan.

i_next_level.title: Next level: plan around delays
i_next_level.detail: Next time, write down which news could matter later and check it every week. Timing your moves around market lag is the next skill to master.

s_savings.title: Your safe money worked too
s_savings.detail: The savings vault paid you {interest} in interest without any risk, and you finished with {savings} in it.

s_savings_rent.title: Your savings paid the rent
s_savings_rent.detail: In Week {week} your cash was short, so {amount} moved automatically from savings to cover the {rent} rent. That is exactly what a bill buffer is for.

i_bought_bad_news.title: You bought into bad news
i_bought_bad_news.detail: In Week {buy_week} you bought {ticker} even though '{event}' (Week {source_week}) had already warned about it - in Week {trigger_week} it hit the price ({impact}), about {loss} on your shares.

evicted.title: Out of Cash
evicted.reason: You couldn't pay the rent in Week {week}. Bills always come before investments.

fomo.title: FOMO Victim
fomo.reason: In Week {week} you {action} {ticker} without checking what the headline really meant, and the season ended at {roi}.

all_in.title: All-In Gambler
all_in.reason: Too much rode on {ticker} - one bad week can undo a whole season ({roi}).

rookie.title: Back to Training
rookie.reason: The season ended at {roi}. Losing play money is the cheapest way to learn - the two weeks below show where.

careful_saver.title: Careful Saver
careful_saver.reason: You protected your money and never missed a bill ({roi}). Next step: let a small part of it work.

prudent.title: Prudent Strategist
prudent.reason: You read the news, kept money ready for the bills and grew your savings by {roi}.

bold.title: Bold Strategist
bold.reason: Big bets paid off this time ({roi}) - keep a bill buffer so one surprise can't sink you.

steady.title: Steady Hand
steady.reason: No disasters and every bill paid ({roi}) - a solid base to build on.

emergency_fund.title: Build a bills buffer first
emergency_fund.habit: Keep at least one month of rent and bills in a separate savings account before you invest anything. Most banks let you open one in a few minutes in their app.

cooling_off.title: Sleep on hot tips
cooling_off.habit: Before you buy because of a viral post or a hot tip, wait 24 hours and check two independent sources. Real news is still true tomorrow.

spread.title: Spread your savings
spread.habit: Never keep all your savings in one company. A fund that holds many companies spreads the risk for you.

check_health.title: Read the hard numbers
check_health.habit: Before you invest in a company, look at its debt and cash, not just the headlines. Rising debt with shrinking cash is a warning light.

automate.title: Pay yourself first
automate.habit: Set up an automatic transfer to a savings account for the day your income arrives - even a small amount grows with interest, and you never forget it.

review_monthly.title: A monthly money check-up
review_monthly.habit: Once a month, open your bank statement: list your fixed bills, see what you saved and only then decide what to invest.

fees.title: Count the fees
fees.habit: Every trade or transfer can cost a fee. Check your bank's price list once and plan fewer, bigger moves instead of many small ones.
